project: Pointed Order Zeta: Artin–Kummer Spectra of Reduction Orders
frozen_definitions: Initial base a is a nonzero integer, a != ±1, initially not a perfect power.
For primes p not dividing a, ord_p(a) is the multiplicative order of a modulo p.
Residual index: I_a(p) = (p - 1) / ord_p(a) = [F_p^x : <a mod p>].
Starting Euler product: Z_a(s,z) = product_{p not dividing a} (1 - I_a(p)^(-z) p^(-s))^(-1).
Initial rigorous domain: real z >= 0 and Re(s) > 1; no analytic continuation is assumed.
Provisional spectrum: Delta_a(z) = lim_{x->infinity} (1/pi(x)) sum_{p<=x, p not dividing a} I_a(p)^(-z), whenever the limit exists.
Kummer fields for the derivation target: K_n(a) = Q(zeta_n, a^(1/n)), subject to perfect-power and entanglement caveats.
foundational_results: For p not dividing a, ord_p(a) divides p-1 and I_a(p) is [F_p^x:<a>].
For n >= 1 and p not dividing a: n | I_a(p) iff n | (p-1) and a mod p is an n-th power in F_p^x.
For fixed n and p not dividing a*n: n | I_a(p) iff p splits completely in K_n(a)=Q(zeta_n,a^(1/n)).
The non-perfect-power hypothesis is not needed for the fixed-n splitting equivalence; it matters for degree formulas and later constants.
For fixed n, Chebotarev gives density 1/[K_n(a):Q] for n | I_a(p), up to a finite exceptional set.
For any arithmetic f, f(I_a(p)) = sum_{n | I_a(p)} (mu*f)(n), pointwise finitely.
For f_z(n)=n^(-z), g_z=mu*f_z is multiplicative and g_z(q^k)=q^(-kz)-q^(-(k-1)z).
For z=0, g_0 is epsilon; for fixed n, g_z(n) tends to mu(n) as z tends to +infinity.
For z >= 0 and Re(s)>1, the Euler product and logarithmic double series are absolutely controlled by zeta(Re(s)).
open_questions: Which generalized Artin / residual-index theorems already contain the fixed-n criterion and averages of general f(I_a(p))?
What exact formulas and uniform lower bounds are known for [Q(zeta_n,a^(1/n)):Q], including perfect-power cases?
What entanglement corrections are needed when degrees are factorized or several Kummer layers are combined?
What hypotheses justify exchanging the infinite Mobius expansion with the prime-density limit?
For which real or complex z does Delta_a(z) exist, and is its degree-series expression already standard?
Does log Z_a(s,z) have leading singular coefficient Delta_a(z) as s -> 1+?
Can Z_a(s,z), or a normalized/logarithmic-derivative variant, be factorized using Dedekind or Artin L-functions from the Kummer tower?
Is I_a(p)^(-z) the most canonical transform of residual index?
Does a nontrivial pointed algebraic-group or 1-motive generalization survive after the G_m case is understood?
killed_conjectures: Naive shorthand: a mod p is an n-th power iff n divides I_a(p), without also requiring n divides p-1. This is false when n does not divide p-1.
